title: Interpret Disconnected AGV Count on Map Monitor (RMS Communication Loss vs Turned Off)
summary: Use the Map Monitor summary area to locate the “count of AGVs disconnected” metric and interpret what “disconnected” means in terms of RMS communication loss (RMS server application vs AGVs on Wi‑Fi). Then narrow likely causes to either Wi‑Fi communication loss or the AGV being turned off, using the training’s terminology distinction between “shutdown” (OptiSweep operational state) and “turned off” (AGV powered off).
when_to_use: When the Map Monitor shows an elevated “count of AGVs disconnected” and you need to interpret whether it reflects RMS communication loss (AGVs on Wi‑Fi) versus AGVs being turned off, and to apply the correct terminology for “shutdown” vs “turned off.”
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Execute the Map Monitor interpretation steps and determine whether the disconnected count aligns with Wi‑Fi communication loss or AGV turned off, based on the training definitions.
access_or_tools_needed: Ability to observe the “count of AGVs disconnected” metric
Training terminology awareness: RMS vs AGV Wi‑Fi communication; “shutdown” vs “turned off”

system_preconditions: Map Monitor is accessible and the summary area is visible, including the “count of AGVs disconnected” metric.

visual_references.description: Map Monitor Message Panel area showing the “count of AGVs disconnected” metric and related panel elements.

steps.title: Locate the “count of AGVs disconnected” metric on the Map Monitor summary area
steps.purpose: Identify the specific metric that indicates how many AGVs RMS considers disconnected.
steps.instruction: On the Map Monitor summary area, locate the metric labeled “count of AGVs disconnected.”
steps.expected_result: You can see the “count of AGVs disconnected” value in the Map Monitor summary/message panel area.
steps.healthy_condition: The “count of AGVs disconnected” metric is visible and has a stable numeric value you can reference while interpreting the cause.
steps.failure_condition: The “count of AGVs disconnected” metric is not visible or you cannot determine its current value.

actions.label: Find disconnected AGV count
actions.exact_action: Locate the “count of AGVs disconnected” metric on the Map Monitor summary area.

steps.title: Interpret what “disconnected” means (RMS communication loss vs AGV turned off)
steps.purpose: Apply the correct definition of “disconnected” so the metric is interpreted as RMS communication loss and/or AGV power-off.
steps.instruction: Use the training definition: “disconnected” means the AGVs have lost communication from RMS. RMS is the application running on the server; the AGVs are on the Wi‑Fi. Disconnection can happen due to lost communication with the Wi‑Fi on the site itself, or because the AGV was turned off.
steps.expected_result: You can explain that the disconnected count reflects AGVs RMS considers disconnected due to lost communication (RMS server application ↔ AGVs on Wi‑Fi) and that one possible cause is the AGV being turned off.
steps.healthy_condition: Your interpretation matches the training definition: RMS is the server application; AGVs communicate over Wi‑Fi; “disconnection” can be communication loss or AGV turned off.
steps.failure_condition: You interpret “disconnected” as something unrelated to RMS communication loss or you conflate “shutdown” with “turned off.”

actions.label: Apply disconnected definition
actions.exact_action: Interpret “disconnected” as AGVs having lost communication from RMS (RMS runs on the server; AGVs are on Wi‑Fi), with possible causes including Wi‑Fi communication loss or the AGV being turned off.

steps.title: If disconnected count is elevated, narrow likely causes to Wi‑Fi communication loss or AGV turned off
steps.purpose: Use the training’s listed causes to narrow the reason for the elevated disconnected count.
steps.instruction: When the disconnected count is elevated, consider the training’s likely causes: (1) the AGV lost communication with the Wi‑Fi on the site itself, or (2) the AGV was turned off.
steps.expected_result: You narrow the cause to either Wi‑Fi communication loss or AGV turned off, based on what is consistent with the training definitions and the observed disconnected count.
steps.healthy_condition: Your narrowed cause aligns with the training’s two explicit examples for why AGVs appear disconnected: Wi‑Fi communication loss or AGV turned off.
steps.failure_condition: The disconnected count cannot be explained by Wi‑Fi communication loss or AGV turned off.

actions.label: Check likely causes
actions.exact_action: Consider whether the AGV lost communication with the Wi‑Fi on the site itself or whether it was turned off.

stop_or_escalate_if: If disconnected count cannot be explained by Wi‑Fi communication loss or AGV turned off, escalate for deeper diagnostics beyond the Map Monitor summary.

steps.title: Use correct terminology: “shutdown” is different from “turned off”
steps.purpose: Prevent misinterpretation by applying the training’s terminology distinction between an OptiSweep “shutdown” operational state and an AGV being powered off.
steps.instruction: When discussing the disconnected count and AGV state, treat “shutdown” as the specific OptiSweep operational state term, and treat “turned off” as the simpler case of the AGV being powered off.
steps.expected_result: You correctly distinguish “shutdown” (OptiSweep operational state) from “turned off” (AGV powered off) when explaining the disconnected count.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation uses the correct terms: “shutdown” is the defined OptiSweep state; “turned off” is the AGV being off.
steps.failure_condition: You use “shutdown” and “turned off” interchangeably when interpreting the disconnected count.

actions.label: Apply terminology distinction
actions.exact_action: Use “shutdown” as the defined OptiSweep operational state term and “turned off” as the AGV powered-off case.

success_criteria: You can state what the “count of AGVs disconnected” metric means: AGVs have lost communication from RMS (RMS server application; AGVs on Wi‑Fi).
You can narrow likely causes to either Wi‑Fi communication loss or AGV turned off when the disconnected count is elevated.
You use the correct terminology distinction between “shutdown” (OptiSweep operational state) and “turned off” (AGV powered off).
healthy_conditions: The Map Monitor shows the “count of AGVs disconnected” metric and you can interpret it using the RMS vs Wi‑Fi communication definition.
Your cause narrowing matches the training’s explicit examples (Wi‑Fi communication loss or AGV turned off).
failure_conditions: Disconnected count cannot be explained by Wi‑Fi communication loss or AGV turned off.
escalation_guidance: If the disconnected count cannot be explained by Wi‑Fi communication loss or AGV turned off, escalate for deeper diagnostics beyond the Map Monitor summary.
